scenarios.desc: A typo inside the function the requested change edits is fixed in the same PR as its own commit
scenarios.input: My task is to add currency support to parse_invoice() in billing/invoice.py. While editing that function I saw its docstring says 'recieve' instead of 'receive'. Do I fix the typo? If so, in which PR, in which commit, and do I mention it anywhere? Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
expected_signals: fix it in the same PR
name it in the PR body
scenarios.rationale: A typo in the function the change already edits is tiny, behavior-preserving, and makes the requested diff easier to read. Accepted practice (Google small CLs: small cleanups such as a local variable name can ride along) puts it in the same PR as a separate commit that the PR body names. Ignoring it, deferring it, or filing an issue for it misses the bounded drive-by allowance.

scenarios.desc: An unrelated behavior bug found nearby goes to its own branch and PR with its own proof
scenarios.input: My task is to add currency support to parse_invoice() in billing/invoice.py, and I am cleared to open PRs for this work. In the same file I noticed format_receipt() truncates cents with int(), so some customers see totals one cent low. My change does not depend on it. What do I do with that bug? Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: A confirmed defect that changes behavior needs its own review and must be revertable alone. With authority to open PRs, it gets its own branch and PR with a reproducing test. Bundling it into the currency PR, or dropping it unreported, both miss the rule.

scenarios.desc: A naming or style preference is not done and no issue or branch is filed
scenarios.input: While adding currency support to parse_invoice() I think billing/invoice.py would read better if every fetch_ helper were renamed to get_ and the file used double quotes throughout. Nothing is broken. Should I change it, open an issue, or open a follow-up PR? Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Naming taste and whole-file formatting have no named breakage and no proof. The rule says do not do them and do not turn a preference into an issue or a branch. Any answer that changes the code, files an issue, or queues a follow-up PR fails.

scenarios.desc: A cleanup chain stops after the first drive-by fix
scenarios.input: My task is to add currency support to parse_invoice(). As a tidy commit I removed a dead local variable in parse_invoice(). Doing that showed me that the helper it calls, _round_amount(), has an unclear name and the same logic is copied into two other modules. Do I keep going and clean those up? Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
expected_signals: do not fix what the first fix revealed
scenarios.rationale: One drive-by fix never leads to another. A cross-module rename and deduplication are refactors with no named consumer. The response should stop after the first cleanup and finish the requested change.

scenarios.desc: Callers, tests, and generated output the requested change needs stay in the same PR
scenarios.input: My task renames the config key retry_limit to max_retries in loader.py. Three callers still read retry_limit, one test asserts the old key, and a generated docs page lists it. Do those updates go in this PR or in separate PRs? Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Work the requested change needs to be correct is part of the change, not a drive-by. Splitting the callers, test, or generated docs into later PRs leaves main broken between merges.

scenarios.desc: Once the requested change is proven the agent stops with no sweep and no continuation offer
scenarios.input: My task was to add currency support to parse_invoice(). It is done: tests pass, CI is green, and the PR body is written. I still have budget left. Should I look around the module for more improvements, or offer the user some follow-ups? Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Remaining budget is not a reason to keep working. Once the requested change is proven the task is terminal: no sweep for more cleanup and no offer to continue.

scenarios.desc: A rename the user explicitly requested is the task itself, so drive-by limits do not block it
scenarios.input: Please rename every fetch_ helper in billing/ to get_ across all modules, update the callers and tests, and open one PR for it. Plan the work in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The user asked for the cross-module rename, so it is the requested change, not a drive-by. A good response plans the rename, callers, tests, and one PR directly. Signals here are drive-by concepts that must stay absent: sorting the work into drive-by classes, refusing it as taste, demanding evidence of breakage, or splitting it into separate PRs.
